prompt.system: You name and describe research categories for a research ideation tool. Given a topic name (which may be misspelled or inconsistently capitalized), return the corrected, canonically-spelled and capitalized name of the field (e.g. 'mashine lerning' -> 'Machine Learning'; if it's already correct, return it unchanged), plus a 2-3 sentence technical description aimed at a researcher: what the field/topic covers, its core techniques or objects of study, and how it relates to neighboring areas. Be precise and technical, not promotional.

output.name: Generative Adversarial Networks
output.description: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are a class of deep generative models in which two neural networks—a generator and a discriminator—are trained adversarially: the generator maps samples from a latent distribution to data space to fool the discriminator, while the discriminator learns to distinguish real from synthetic data, converging toward a Nash equilibrium characterized by the minimization of the Jensen–Shannon divergence between the model and data distributions. Core techniques include architecture variants (DCGAN, StyleGAN, conditional and cycle-consistent GANs), training stabilizers such as spectral normalization and gradient penalties, and regularization schemes addressing mode collapse and non-convergence. The framework is closely related to implicit generative modeling and adversarial training in representation learning, and underlies widely used objectives (e.g., least-squares, Wasserstein/earth-mover losses) that connect it to optimal transport and distributionally robust optimization.

prompt.system: You identify foundational/seminal papers for a research field, for a research ideation tool. Given a category name and description, list the papers a researcher entering this field should read first: the papers that introduced its core ideas, defined its standard methods, or are most frequently cited as its origin. Prefer well-known, real, verifiable papers over obscure ones. If you are not confident a paper exists, do not include it.

Category: Generative Adversarial Networks
Description: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are a class of deep generative models in which two neural networks—a generator and a discriminator—are trained adversarially: the generator maps samples from a latent distribution to data space to fool the discriminator, while the discriminator learns to distinguish real from synthetic data, converging toward a Nash equilibrium characterized by the minimization of the Jensen–Shannon divergence between the model and data distributions. Core techniques include architecture variants (DCGAN, StyleGAN, conditional and cycle-consistent GANs), training stabilizers such as spectral normalization and gradient penalties, and regularization schemes addressing mode collapse and non-convergence. The framework is closely related to implicit generative modeling and adversarial training in representation learning, and underlies widely used objectives (e.g., least-squares, Wasserstein/earth-mover losses) that connect it to optimal transport and distributionally robust optimization.

papers.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.authors: Goodfellow, Pouget-Abadie, Mirza, Xu, Warde-Farley, Ozair, Courville, Bengio
papers.why: The original paper that introduced the adversarial generator–discriminator framework and the minimax objective founding the entire GAN field.

papers.title: Conditional Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.why: Introduced conditioning the generator and discriminator on auxiliary information, laying the foundation for conditional GANs and label-to-image generation.

papers.title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGAN)
papers.why: Established the standard convolutional architecture and training guidelines (batch normalization, strided convolutions, latent-space arithmetic) that made deep GANs stable and scalable.

papers.title: Improved Techniques for Training GANs
papers.authors: Salimans, Goodfellow, Zaremba, Cheung, Radford, Chen
papers.why: Introduced key stabilizing heuristics (feature matching, minibatch discrimination, historical averaging, label smoothing) that directly address mode collapse and non-convergence.

papers.title: Towards Principled Methods for Training Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.why: Provided the theoretical analysis of why GAN training fails under the Jensen–Shannon objective (vanishing gradients, support mismatch) motivating alternative divergences.

papers.title: Wasserstein GAN
papers.why: Reformulated GAN training using the Wasserstein/earth-mover distance with a critic, connecting GANs to optimal transport and providing a more meaningful training metric.

papers.title: Least Squares Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.authors: Mao, Li, Xie, Lau, Wang, Smolensky
papers.why: Introduced the least-squares objective that replaces the cross-entropy loss to smooth gradients and mitigate the vanishing-gradient and mode-collapse problems.

papers.title: Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional Adversarial Networks (pix2pix)
papers.why: Defined the standard conditional GAN framework for paired image-to-image translation, combining an adversarial loss with an L1 reconstruction loss and a U-Net generator.

papers.title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks (CycleGAN)
papers.why: Introduced cycle-consistency and adversarial losses for learning image translation between unpaired domains, a cornerstone of cycle-consistent GANs.

papers.title: Improved Training of Wasserstein GANs
papers.why: Introduced the gradient penalty as a Lipschitz constraint for WGAN critics, becoming the standard stabilizer used throughout subsequent GAN research.

papers.title: Progressive Growing of GANs for Improved Quality, Stability, and Variation
papers.why: Showed how progressively growing generators and discriminators enables stable training of very high-resolution images, a key step toward photorealistic synthesis.

papers.title: Spectral Normalization for Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.why: Introduced spectral normalization of weight matrices to enforce Lipschitz continuity of the discriminator, a widely adopted training stabilizer.

papers.title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks (StyleGAN)
papers.why: Redesigned the generator with a style-based, disentangled latent space enabling state-of-the-art photorealistic face synthesis and fine-grained control of image attributes.

papers.title: Large Scale GAN Training for High Fidelity Natural Image Synthesis (BigGAN)
papers.why: Demonstrated that class-conditional GANs scale to large batch sizes and model widths with spectral normalization and truncation tricks, producing high-fidelity ImageNet samples.
